claims.text: Adding a small amount of yttrium to a refractory high-entropy alloy can improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The proposed intervention applies to refractory high-entropy alloys in an as-cast or wrought state.
The intervention is the addition of a small, unspecified amount of yttrium to the alloy composition.
The yttrium modification should be effective above 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Adding yttrium promotes formation of a protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer may contain Y2O3.
The protective oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion reduces the alloy's oxidation rate.
A reduced oxidation rate improves high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to the yttrium-free alloy.
The cited records discuss relationships between alloy microstructure and material properties under elevated-temperature or other extreme conditions.
The cited records support the role of protective surface oxide layers in controlling oxygen diffusion.
Yttrium addition could increase service life and reduce maintenance costs.
The protective layer will cease to be effective beyond some maximum temperature or oxygen partial pressure.
The experiment should compare otherwise comparable refractory high-entropy alloys with and without yttrium using high-temperature oxidation testing.
Thermogravimetry and scanning electron microscopy can be used to measure oxidation rate, oxide-layer thickness, and microstructural evolution.
Failure of the yttrium-containing alloy to show a significant improvement in oxidation rate and oxide-layer thickness relative to the untreated alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
